speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how many days have you had the fever and wrist pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (caused by Borrelia burgdorferi infection).

The patient's recent camping trip in Minnesota, history of self-resolving knee pain, and current presentation of fever, chills, and a monoarticular swollen wrist are highly characteristic of disseminated Lyme disease. Given the severity and the specific joint involvement, this is likely the most probable diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology (ELISA followed by Western Blot).
REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential and ESR.
REQUEST TEST: Synovial_Fluid_Analysis (Left Wrist).
